--------
Former Brooklyn drug kingpin and enforcer Brian “Glaze” Gibbs returns to VladTV to discuss his violent past, cooperation with the government, major hip-hop criminal cases, and the transformation that ultimately led him away from the streets.

Gibbs reflects on his criminal history during the 1980s, openly discussing his involvement in five murders and being acquitted of a sixth. He breaks down his cooperation with federal authorities and his 5K1 letter, explaining how prosecutors from Brooklyn and Queens attempted to question him about additional unsolved murders. He also reflects on the death of his mother, which became a major turning point that forced him to confront the damage caused by his lifestyle.

The conversation shifts to Keefe D’s Tupac murder trial, with Gibbs discussing Keefe D’s decision to reject a 10-to-25-year plea deal at 63 years old. While viewing him as an underdog, Gibbs believes Keefe D could ultimately become the person held responsible for one of hip-hop’s most infamous murders.

Vlad and Gibbs also examine several other high-profile cases, including the murder-for-hire case involving Quando Rondo, the latest developments surrounding the murder of Jam Master Jay, and the convictions and pleas involving Ronald Washington, Karl Jordan Jr., and Jay Bryant. They also revisit the notorious kidnapping and murder of Rich Porter’s younger brother, discussing the extreme violence surrounding New York’s drug era.

Gibbs concludes by explaining how he escaped the criminal mentality that once controlled his life. Now focused on health, fitness, family, and legitimate business, he discusses his upcoming book and a potential screenplay project involving LL Cool J. His message to younger generations is simple: street money and reputation are temporary, while the consequences can last forever.

recentItems.title: Lul Tim on How He'd Feel if Lil Durk Got Death Penalty for Killing His Friend Lul Pab (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback, Lul Tim discussed his feelings about the legal troubles surrounding fellow artist Lil Durk, who is facing serious charges connected to the murder of Lul Tim’s friend, Lul Pab. When asked about the possibility of Durk facing life in prison or the death penalty, Lul Tim expressed a sense of resignation, saying that the outcome is ultimately in “God’s hands.” He emphasized that he doesn’t wish ill will on anyone and would rather leave the matter to fate and the legal process. Despite the gravity of the situation, Lul Tim reflected on the emotional complexities of seeing someone he knows face such serious consequences.

Attorney Moe Gangat returns to VladTV with a firsthand courtroom breakdown from Los Angeles, where he has been covering Lil Durk’s federal trial since day one. Gangat details the direct examination of cooperating witness OTF Vonnie, real name Kayvon Grant, who testified about his guilty plea and alleged role in the 2022 killing of Lil Pab near the Beverly Center, as well as a prior shootout tied to Quando Rondo in Blackshear, Georgia. The discussion covers alleged OTF connections, King Von, THF Zoo, OTF Jam, DD, Chicago associates, stolen cars, guns, ski masks, surveillance footage, and travel through Miami, San Diego, Encino, and LA. Gangat also explains how investigators may have built the case through clues like “Rags to Riches” clothing, BMW tracking data, and cooperation from OTF Jam. A detailed legal analysis of testimony, strategy, and what it could mean for Durk’s defense.

Hit-Boy sits down with Elliott Wilson and Vlad to unpack the hard lessons behind building a music empire while trying to lift up family and friends. The Grammy-winning producer explains why he’s shifted toward film and TV scoring, where the business feels cleaner than chasing rapper album placements and delayed upfront fees.

He reflects on his Interscope deal, sacrificing beats that could have gone to Kanye West and major artists, and spending millions on homies, his father Big Hit, and his sister HitgirlLENA’s rap ambitions. From a Tarzana house full of studios to missed momentum with K Roosevelt’s “Dummy” on Power 106, Hit-Boy breaks down loyalty, timing, and why talent development can become emotionally and financially draining.

The conversation also touches L.A. Reid, Clive Davis, LaFace Records, Whitney Houston, Outkast, DJ Premier, North Carolina, and the realities of mixing family with business.

Judge Mathis joins VladTV to break down key issues in the federal case involving Lil Durk, OTF, and allegations tied to Quando Rondo. The discussion focuses on OTF Jam’s credibility as a cooperating witness, possible contradictions in his testimony, and how a jury may view claims made by people seeking reduced time. Mathis also analyzes reports about OTF Vonnie taking the stand, alleged conversations at the studio, and whether prosecutors have direct evidence—such as audio or texts—connecting Durk to a claimed $1 million offer. Vlad and Mathis examine the defense angle, including arguments that any alleged order may have been interpreted as a beatdown rather than murder, while noting Durk was not accused of being a shooter or present at the scene. A legal-minded look at testimony, cooperation, and reasonable doubt in a closely watched hip-hop trial.

Charleston White sits down with Vlad to break down the upcoming Dallas murder trial connected to Mo3’s killing, discussing prosecutors’ claims involving Kewon White, Devin Brown, Jocelyn Jackson, alleged payments, bank records, and how Yella Beezy could be tied into the case. White argues that the jury may weigh Dallas politics, Mo3’s legacy, music videos, lyrics, and courtroom testimony heavily — and says Yella Beezy may need to testify if he wants to avoid a guilty verdict.

The conversation also touches on the role of rap lyrics in court, friends allegedly mocking deaths online, Earl Spence, Hurricane Chris winning his self-defense case after taking the stand, and broader legal realities facing artists like Lil Durk amid street-related allegations. Vlad and Charleston debate whether silence helps or hurts defendants in murder cases, accountability under the law, and why fame, money, and street beef can become a dangerous mix in hip-hop.

recentItems.title: Lul Tim Reacts to Lil Durk's Murder-for-Hire Arrest for Killing His Friend Lul Pab (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, Lul Tim weighed in on the high-profile arrest of Lil Durk and five others in connection with an alleged murder-for-hire plot that resulted in the killing of Lul Pab. According to federal prosecutors, the alleged operation involved suspects traveling from Chicago to San Diego, as well as a private flight from Miami to Los Angeles, with funding allegedly tied to Lil Durk.

The indictment detailed an elaborate series of arrangements involving flights, accommodations, rental vehicles, and the alleged purchase of weapons. However, prosecutors say the plot ultimately resulted in the killing of the wrong person, with Lul Pab being fatally shot at a gas station.

Lul Tim criticized the alleged operation as "sloppy work," pointing to the extensive paper trail left behind by those involved. Amid the public controversy and online reactions, Tim reflected on the bigger picture, arguing that the situation illustrates the destructive cycle of violence, retaliation, and legal trouble that continues to affect the hip-hop community.
